recipes.title: Spinach Carbonara with Mozzarella
recipes.pitch: A salty, satisfying way to use up that spinach before it wilts, plus all those eggs
steps: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the spaghetti according to packet instructions. Reserve a mugful of pasta cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the bacon or pancetta and fry for 5 minutes until crisp. Remove and set aside.
Wilt the spinach in the same pan with a splash of water for 2 minutes, then remove excess liquid.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with most of the parmesan or mozzarella and plenty of black pepper.

Return the spaghetti to the pan off the heat. Pour over the egg mixture and toss well, adding reserved pasta water a little at a time until glossy and coating the pasta. The residual heat should cook the eggs gently without scrambling.
Stir through the bacon and spinach. Serve topped with mozzarella, reserved cheese and extra black pepper.

recipes.title: Broccoli & Spinach Soup with Lemon
recipes.pitch: A vibrant green soup that saves wilting spinach and that head of broccoli, lifted with fresh lemon
steps: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the broccoli florets and baby carrots, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 800ml water and crumble in a stock cube if using. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 10-12 minutes until the broccoli is tender.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Blend the soup until very smooth using a hand blender. Stir in a splash of milk for creaminess if you like, and a good squeeze of lemon juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve in warm bowls with a drizzle of olive oil and torn mozzarella on top if using.

recipes.title: Roasted Eggplant, Tomato & Mozzarella Traybake
recipes.pitch: Sweet roasted tomatoes and soft aubergine topped with melting mozzarella – a fresh, summery traybake
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Lightly oil a large roasting tray.

Slice the eggplants and zucchini into 1cm rounds. Arrange on the tray with the cherry tomatoes and thickly sliced tomatoes. Drizzle with oil, season with salt, pepper and a pinch of chilli flakes or dried herbs if you have them.
Roast for 20-22 minutes until the vegetables are soft and starting to caramelise at the edges.
Tear the mozzarella over the top and return to the oven for 3-4 minutes until just melted.
Serve straight from the tray with a squeeze of lemon or lime juice and an extra drizzle of oil. Great on its own or with crusty bread to mop up the juices.
